title: ORBIT-FMIB: Tracking Order-Resolved Epistatic Information Through ESM-2
abstract: arXiv:2610.00672v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Protein foundation models support mutation-effect and structural prediction, but predictive performance alone does not reveal which forms of biological interaction information remain accessible through model depth. We ask whether ESM-2 retains higher-order epistatic information as strongly as first- and second-order information across its representation hierarchy, introducing ORBIT-FMIB, a diagnostic framework combining Walsh-based interaction decomposition with subset-conditioned neural dependence estimation. The method is validated on synthetic landscapes with known interaction structure before being applied to the dense four-site GB1 fitness landscape using frozen ESM-2 representations.   An initial production run suggested ESM-2 retains higher-order epistatic information less well than lower-order information ($\Delta_{\mathrm{HO-LO}}=-0.107$). translated_title: ORBIT-FMIB：追踪ESM-2中的阶数分辨上位性信息
translated_abstract: 蛋白质基础模型支持突变效应预测和结构预测，但仅凭预测性能并不能揭示哪些形式的生物学相互作用信息在模型深层中仍然可及。我们探究ESM-2在其表示层次结构中是否像一阶和二阶信息那样强地保留高阶上位性信息，并由此提出ORBIT-FMIB——一个将基于Walsh函数的相互作用分解与子集条件化神经依赖性估计相结合的诊断框架。该方法首先在具有已知相互作用结构的合成适应度景观上进行验证，随后利用冻结的ESM-2表示应用于密集的四位点GB1适应度景观。初步生产运行结果表明，ESM-2对高阶上位性信息的保留能力弱于低阶信息（Δ_HO-LO = -0.107）。在匹配的GPU硬件条件下，对完整测量网格的独立复现……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出ORBIT-FMIB诊断框架，结合Walsh相互作用分解与子集条件化神经依赖性估计，系统测量发现ESM-2在其表示层次中对高阶上位性信息的保留能力弱于低阶信息。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces ORBIT-FMIB, a diagnostic framework combining Walsh-based interaction decomposition with subset-conditioned neural dependence estimation, and finds that ESM-2 retains higher-order epistatic information less well than lower-order information across its representation hierarchy.
